statement.p: Calculate the flux of the vector field \vec F=(x^2+y^2)\vec k through the disk of radius 5 in the xy-plane and centered at the origin and oriented in the direction of the positive z axis.

static.solution: D, is in the xy-plane and oriented in the direction of the positive z axis, d\vec A=\vec k\, dx\, dy and \int_{D} \vec F\cdot d\vec A = \int_{D} (x^2+y^2)\vec k\cdot \vec k\, dx\,dy = \int_{D}(x^2+y^2)\, dx\,dy. Using polar coordinates (with x = r\cos\theta and y = r\sin\theta), \int_{D}\vec F\cdot d\vec A = \int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{5} r^2\cdot r\, dr\,d\theta = 2\pi \left.\frac {r^4}4\right|_0^{5} = \frac{625\pi}{2}.
